## 2026-09-20 — Contract-enforced ETL and deterministic provenance

Discovery used three materially different modes: analog search from the current Floe/OpenLineage/Polyglot leaders; code/file/protocol searches around fail-closed contracts, quarantine, fingerprints, lineage and schema evolution; and obscure low-attention orchestration projects. One new candidate cleared the bar in this lane.

### RaghavBanuni/data-pipeline-orchestration-contracts — STRONG — 26/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/RaghavBanuni/data-pipeline-orchestration-contracts
- Exact revision: `624ade383f7c202d27b865640ad34f603946292e`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component
- Concrete capability: Python-standard-library pipeline engine with dependency DAG execution, content-addressed incremental recomputation, task/code/contract/config/partition/output fingerprints, early cutoff when outputs are unchanged, enforceable data contracts, schema-evolution checks, data-quality rules, retry budgets, a durable SQLite WAL/FULL run ledger, dataset/column lineage and publish-after-validation semantics. Contracts support FAIL_CLOSED, QUARANTINE and WARN behavior rather than silently coercing bad inputs.
- Rare / undernoticed value: The unusual combination is reproducibility plus enforcement: the same engine decides whether work is stale, whether output satisfies a contract, whether rows should quarantine, and what exact upstream/code/config state produced a published result. That is a useful evidence primitive for money-bearing pipelines where malformed or drifted data must not silently become a claim.
- Buyer/problem: Data-platform teams, regulated SaaS, finance/audit products and vertical applications that have brittle Python/data jobs but need deterministic reruns, schema-change safety, provenance and explainable publication gates.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Fixed-price trusted-pipeline hardening diagnostic: wrap one existing customer-authorized ingestion/transformation flow with fingerprints, contract enforcement, quarantine and lineage receipts, then convert to managed data-quality/lineage monitoring.
- Build-time/data advantage: Roughly 3–6 months of DAG, fingerprint, state-ledger, contract, retry, lineage and test engineering compressed for a lightweight embedded runtime.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision; README; MIT root license; substantive modules for DAG/executor/fingerprint/contracts/ledger/lineage/quality/retry; dedicated tests for contracts, DAG behavior, executor, fingerprints, ledger, lineage, quality and retry semantics. The implementation is local/embedded rather than a mature warehouse-connector ecosystem, so it complements rather than replaces Floe/OpenLineage.
- Actual public license/rights: MIT, verified from root `LICENSE`. External databases/datasets and any production customer data remain separately governed.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is also treated as separately commercially authorized under the standing user assertion; no implied rights extend to third-party data/services.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable permissive infrastructure; strongest as an embedded contract/provenance engine rather than a standalone enterprise orchestrator.
- Score: A3 speed / B4 ceiling / C5 compression / D4 rarity / E5 evidence / F5 rights clarity = **26/30**.
- Combination opportunities: `DriftGuard -> Floe -> data-pipeline-orchestration-contracts -> Polyglot/sqllens -> OpenLineage -> Stitch` creates a stronger chain from schema-change prevention through runtime acceptance/quarantine, deterministic recomputation and transformation lineage to controlled downstream remediation. Freight/AP/CaptureBrief can reuse the same publication invariant: unresolved contract or quality failure never becomes a money-bearing fact.
- Next action: Run a synthetic invoice/vendor ETL fixture with schema drift, one quarantined row, one code change, one unchanged-output rerun and one interrupted retry; verify deterministic fingerprints, ledger state, column lineage and publish gating, then map the lineage receipt into OpenLineage facets.

## 2026-09-20 — Canonical document evidence graphs and underwriting-grade extraction

Discovery used analog searches seeded from Zerox/Docpipe/Veridoc/Assay, code/file searches around bbox/source-page/confidence/review lineage and reconciliation, and deliberately obscure vertical/standards projects. Five candidates were materially inspected; four are strong and one is watch.

### eigenpal/openparser — STRONG / MASTER CONTENDER — 29/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/eigenpal/openparser
- Exact revision: `29472999c65041991b2ca401b2d44c333e99e652`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Apache-2.0 document-normalization monorepo that converts heterogeneous OCR/document-AI provider output into a common `openparser@1` representation, with schema, lineage, provider adapters, CLI and TypeScript/Python SDKs. The lineage package models a complete derivation DAG based on W3C PROV-DM with strict references, unique-producer and acyclicity validation, append-only history, review events and first-class confidence assertions. Provider adapters include Paddle HPS, Mistral OCR, Azure Document Intelligence, Google Document AI and AWS Textract while preserving hierarchy, spans, coordinate spaces, styles, languages, tables, fields, image assets and native source granularity.
- Rare / undernoticed value: It attacks the hardest portability/evidence problem in document AI: preserving provider-specific geometry and evidence while presenting one canonical graph to downstream code. Confidence is explicitly typed by origin/method/scope/granularity/calibration rather than treated as one universally comparable float, and uncalibrated provider scores are not silently equated.
- Buyer/problem: Document-AI vendors, audit/recovery products, regulated workflow builders and enterprises switching OCR providers without wanting to rewrite review/provenance logic or lose source evidence.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Fixed-price document-provider normalization/migration diagnostic: run the same authorized document set through two existing extractors, normalize both into OpenParser, compare grounding/review evidence and deliver a provider-portability report; later sell an embedded evidence gateway.
- Build-time/data advantage: Plausibly 6–12+ months of canonical schema, provider adapters, evidence DAG, review semantics, SDK and conformance-test engineering compressed.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision README; Apache-2.0 root license; dedicated lineage README documenting W3C-PROV-inspired DAG validation and confidence semantics; adapter README documenting provider-specific preservation; substantial source/test tree including grounding/lineage/review tests, schema validation, provider fixtures and SDK retry/review tests.
- Actual public license/rights: Apache-2.0 for repository-owned code. Cloud OCR APIs, provider outputs, model weights and customer documents remain governed separately.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is treated as separately commercially authorized in addition to Apache-2.0; no implied grant covers providers, models or document rights.
- Reuse classification: High-value canonical document/evidence substrate.
- Score: A4 speed / B5 ceiling / C5 compression / D5 rarity / E5 evidence / F5 rights clarity = **29/30**.
- Combination opportunities: `Zerox/Docpipe/Veridoc/Prismdoc -> OpenParser canonical graph + lineage/review -> Assay selective acceptance -> Floe contract/quarantine -> OpenLineage/Kton`. This gives freight/AP/CaptureBrief/ScopeSignal one portable evidence envelope instead of provider-specific glue.
- Next action: Differential-test 25 synthetic/public multi-format documents through at least two supported providers/adapters and measure evidence conservation: page/bbox/span/table identity, review history, confidence provenance and round-trip loss.

### prxtxks/credexis — STRONG / MASTER CONTENDER — 30/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/prxtxks/credexis
- Exact revision: `de4f350e8b131fd939774f1771d633c0c1be76df`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: Full SBA 7(a) underwriting automation system built around examiner-grade source evidence rather than generic extraction. The inspected README describes two independent extractors that must agree to the exact cent, deterministic reconciliation, six blocking validation gates, IRS-transcript cross-checking, integer-cent calculations, versioned SBA policy packs, append-mostly facts, human override/supersession history, borrower intake, click-to-source bounding boxes and an evaluation corpus. The latest inspected commit improves UNKNOWN-span review by surfacing why the classifier abstained instead of forcing a guess.
- Rare / undernoticed value: Its architectural invariant is unusually strong: every stored number must trace to a page+bbox, IRS transcript line or explicit human input; AI is not allowed to perform money arithmetic, validation failure blocks auto-accept, and edits supersede rather than mutate prior facts. This is a reusable blueprint for any high-stakes document-to-money system.
- Buyer/problem: Community/regional banks and SBA lending teams spend analyst hours re-keying tax/financial packages while needing defensible, examiner-ready lineage months later.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Deploy one lender-authorized SBA spread/review workspace or run a paid acceptance diagnostic on a closed set of historical loans, measuring analyst time, exact-cent agreement, review volume and source-trace completeness before any production decision use.
- Build-time/data advantage: More than 12 months of vertical workflow, evidence model, deterministic finance engine, review UX, tenancy/security, evaluation and policy-versioning engineering compressed.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision and recent commit history; README documenting architecture, 64k TypeScript LOC, 834 tests and 76 RLS attack scenarios as project claims; explicit iron laws for integer-cent money, source lineage, append-mostly facts and blocking validation; evaluation/security architecture; public license file. Repository claims remain claims until independently reproduced. No borrower/customer/private data was inspected.
- Actual public license/rights: Public `LICENSE` is source-available/evaluation-only, copyright Uxory LLC, and expressly forbids operating a product/service, modification or distribution without permission; Credexis name/logo are trademarks. Under the standing hunt assumption, the user's separate commercial permission is treated as authorization for repository-owned code for prioritization/product analysis. Trademarks, third-party extraction providers/APIs, IRS access, customer documents and regulated-lending obligations remain separate.
- Reuse classification: Commercial-use candidate only under the user's asserted separate permission; preserve the restrictive public-license provenance and independently diligence third-party/service/regulatory surfaces.
- Score: A5 speed / B5 ceiling / C5 compression / D5 rarity / E5 evidence / F5 reuse clarity under the standing separate-permission assumption = **30/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Generalize Credexis's dual-reader consensus, blocking gates, source-bbox facts and supersession ledger into freight/AP/contract extraction; pair with OpenParser for provider-neutral representation and Assay/ExtractBench for independent acceptance benchmarking. As a vertical, it also suggests a standalone managed SBA underwriting-evidence product rather than only infrastructure reuse.
- Next action: Run an independent rights-clean/synthetic acceptance corpus with planted OCR disagreements, period shifts, arithmetic mismatches and missing pages; verify that no wrong value reaches accepted state and that every accepted money value has reconstructable source/reviewer lineage.

## 2026-09-20 — Stable-key guardrails and ER wrapper triage

Discovery used analog search from GoldenMatch/Splink/Canon/Neotoma, code/file search around human review, cluster IDs and merge/split semantics, and low-attention project discovery. Three new candidates were materially inspected; one is retained as watch and two are rejected to prevent future duplication.

### saharah-99/anchorkey — WATCH — 23/30
- Canonical URL: https://github.com/saharah-99/anchorkey
- Exact revision: `aee066431488f36619c807cdc84333e426f6c9a0`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component
- Concrete capability: Apache-2.0 natural-key normalization/resolution library for identifiers that drift through spacing, case and Unicode variants. It explicitly refuses fuzzy guesses where a string metric cannot distinguish a typo from a genuinely different short identifier, routes unresolved cases to human review, applies effective-dated labels at query time and keeps labels out of the identity derivation so identity remains a reproducible function of content.
- Rare / undernoticed value: The value is conservative anti-overmerge behavior for short/atomic identifiers, not broad entity resolution. It is a useful guardrail before probabilistic matching when an asset code, sensor ID, vendor code or other natural key should normalize deterministically but must not be fuzzily collapsed.
- Buyer/problem: Telemetry/asset/master-data teams and vertical products where small identifier-format changes fragment history, but a false merge is more costly than a review item.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Embed as a normalization/identity-preflight step in a vendor/asset master cleanup diagnostic, showing how many records can be safely normalized without invoking probabilistic linkage.
- Build-time/data advantage: Roughly weeks to 1–2 months of conservative Unicode/key normalization, effective-dated labels, review semantics and property-test design; narrow scope limits standalone value.
- Evidence inspected: Exact revision README; Apache-2.0 license; source/test tree; documented refusal of broad fuzzy matching; property tests for idempotency and limitations; reproducible openSenseMap snapshot/catalog tooling. The repository itself states that broad cross-source identity resolution is out of scope.
- Actual public license/rights: Apache-2.0 for repository code. Public-source snapshots/datasets retain their own provenance/terms and should be regenerated from lawful sources rather than blindly redistributed.
- User-asserted separate commercial-permission posture: Repository-owned public code is treated as separately commercially authorized; third-party/public-source dataset rights remain separate.
- Reuse classification: Narrow but high-integrity normalization primitive; use upstream of Splink/GoldenMatch/Canon rather than as a replacement.
- Score: A3 / B3 / C4 / D4 / E4 / F5 = **23/30**.
- Combination opportunities: `AnchorKey deterministic natural-key normalization -> Splink/GoldenMatch probabilistic linkage -> Canon reviewed registry -> Neotoma durable merge/split state`. This reduces candidate noise and false joins while keeping fuzzy inference away from identifiers that should be content-stable.
- Next action: Test on a synthetic vendor/asset corpus containing safe Unicode/spacing/case variants plus near-collision identifiers; measure safe normalization yield and ensure ambiguous near-collisions remain unresolved.
